In the eerie silence of a roller rink, a man named Clarence met his startling end by a trident, pulling Detective Winston into a web of enmity and suspicion involving two unusual suspects, Unity and Vivian.

The flashing lights of the roller rink danced in a kaleidoscope of colors across Winston's stern face. He always had a knack for ending up in the most bizarre crime scenes, and this one was no different: A man named Clarence ended up dead at a roller rink, and the murder weapon was a trident. His primary suspect was Unity, the tour guide who Clarence had recently discovered was faking her knowledge about maritime history and planning to expose her. 

Gathering himself, he strolled over to the corner, introducing himself to Unity, who was currently explaining to a group of tourists about the different types of tridents on display, her gaze fixated on the cases or wandering the distance, never meeting the eyes of her audience. She had the keys to the exhibits and thus unrestricted access to the tridents, a detail unbeknownst to the onlookers but not to Winston. 

"I understand you’re in charge of this trident exhibit.” Winston pointed to the display case behind her. Unity glanced at the detective, showing a twinkling keychain, nodding. "Yes, sir. I am the keeper of the keys around here," she confirmed, outwardly displaying a pride in her role.

Winston started to probe: "How did you end up in this line of work? You seem young..." Unity took a moment, her gaze dropping to the ground. "You could say it was my destiny," She replied, "I've always been fascinated with the here, pretending to grasp every bit of maritime history...or at least pretending to do so…”

Printfessed, Winston furthered his inquiry. “So, you have exclusive access to these tridents, right?” He meditated her reactions. Unity took a moment, her gaze deflecting to the ground and then at the tourists’ faces. Faking her blithe demeanor, she corroborated, “Indeed, I do. These tridents we have here are from various eras—each belonging to a significant point in history and I am trained to handle them with utmost care. As a tour guide, I am responsible for explaining the heritage and significance of these artifacts.. "

Unity abruptly steered the conversation towards the artefacts and their historical context, evading Winston's direct questions. To an untrained eye, this would've made her look like an industrious professional. But Winston noticed her tactical evasion, making him ponder over how Clarence had noticed the same. He remembered how Clarence had confessed about Unity's deception before his untimely demise, her feigned knowledge about maritime history, her meticulously concealed secret, her meticulously fabricated response. 

Winston decided to step back for a bit, reassess his facts and clues. He had a gut feeling that both Clarence's death and Unity's secret were intertwined that this tour wasn't as benign as it seemed. He knew he was onto something. Unity's pride, her faked knowledge, her training with tridents, her constant evasion... While they weren't direct evidence, they were leading him somewhere.

With hands in his coat pockets, Winston retreated, mind abuzz with the next steps he needed to take in this intriguing roller rink homicide case. All the while under the riotous strobe lights, Unity's voice continued to echo through the space, meticulously detailing the care for tridents, her twisted pride in her position unfaltering. Even as they stood over a murder scene, she maintained the charade, pretending as if nothing had ever happened.

Detective Winston scanned over the vivid crime scene for a moment, the macabre tableau horribly out of place in the otherwise cheery atmosphere of a roller rink. Luminescent skates scattered haphazardly over the checkered floors, their normally playful glow eerily reflecting off pools of crimson. His mind slowly pieced together the events that led up to this, putting a face to the victim - Clarence, a man known for spending his every Wednesday nights weaving his way around this very rink on roller skates, his love for the sport unparalleled.

With a heavy breath, he set towards his first line of inquiry: Vivian, a woman with an affinity to ancient warfare, the campus vendor, who was known more for her expertise in old military tactics than her concessions. He found her behind a small food counter, her arms steady as she meticulously arranged pretzels on a tray.

"Evening, Vivian," he greeted, his tone conspicuously casual.

"Detective," she nodded, not pausing her work. It was clear she respected the gravity the situation held; she just was not going to show it in the middle of her shift.

"I understand you have an impressive collection of historical artifacts, some of which include ancient weaponry?" Winston broached the subject delicately.

"Yes," she conceded, keeping her gaze lowered. "One of the weapons being a trident, if I recall correctly."

Vivian froze momentarily, to draw breath or collect her thoughts, he couldn't discern. "Yes, that's correct. I even attended some trident handling courses last summer, part of an educational experience," she clarified, her tone suddenly defensive.

"Interesting," Winston said breezily, not wanting to sharpen the conversation's edge any further. "Tell me, Vivian. Is it also true that your sister is your only living relative, and you've had to step in to protect her on a few occasions? Like, when a school bully once tormented her?”

Surprised, Vivian admitted. "Yes, Detective. My sister means everything to me. I stopped that bully, and I would do anything to keep her safe."

Feeling he was making progress, Winston casually unveiled his most delicate inquiry yet, "By the way, your sister stopped by earlier."

Vivian's back stiffened, a spark of alertness crossing her face. "She did?"

"Yeah," Winston replied, trying to suppress any hint of curiosity. "She mentioned she’d spoken to you about Clarence sending her some inappropriate messages? She said it had particularly upset her, knowing how dedicated Clarence is to his Wednesday night skating sessions."

For a moment, Vivian looked cornered, before a veil of resignation fell over her face, "Yes, Detective. We talked about it; she was really upset."

"And you happened to be working that evening when the incident occurred?"

"I was," Vivian answered quietly, wearing an expression Winston could not decipher.

"Interesting night it must've been," Winston commented before bidding Vivian a good night.

As he walked away, he couldn't help the unsettled feeling creeping up his spine. The circumstances were stacking, and the evening's events were beginning to form a disconcertingly clear narrative. But the writing wasn't on the wall. Not yet. It was, after all, a puzzle he needed to piece together nap by nap, with the reader doing much of the deducing. For now, he'd step aside and allow the story to unfold.

Despite such peculiar oddities, something else caught Winston’s attention. Jay's demeanor exhibited an aura of a grieving father who had just lost his child. Every word, every gesture towards Johnny was drenched in fatherly affection. This he observed as he subtly probed into Jay's Times Square hotel booking from that very night shared over their New Year's plans discussion.

Jay confidently produced the confirmation for his hotel reservation, confirming his presence at Times Square, booked for the very night of the murder taking place. Johnny had confessed to him, and unbelievably, Jay happened to overhear their private conversation revealing Johnny's turn of trust.

Despite the city's innumerable faces, battalions of CCTV cameras, incessantly flashing screens surrounding the quadrant, a witness had spotted Karl here.

Clearing his throat, Winston began his interrogation. "You've been spotted here today Karl, can you explain that?"

"You and Johnny had an argument?"

People swarmed around like an ongoing carnival, but Winston kept his gaze unwavered on Karl. "You have a soft spot for history, don't you?" Winston ventured.

"Yeah, I love historical weaponry. I've got a nice collection at home," Karl stated somewhat proudly.

Winston knew, his suspicion was correct. The house search had revealed a Trident among Karl's collection of ancient weapons, now confiscated.

"Interesting," he observed. "Used any of them? For fighting or such."

"Tridents... I took some trident fighting lessons last summer," Karl admitted with an awkward laugh.

Strange coincidence, or just an indication of motives, Winston thought. Besides, the trident and Times Square; there was also that heated argument over some documents about his financial misdemeanors.

"Financial misdemeanors," Winston probed.

The look in Karl's eyes revealed something, but he simply shrugged, "Stock market’s a tricky business, detective. Johnny didn't fully understand it."

Winston thanked him for his time and left. City lights illuminated the square. Karl, now successful in stock manipulation, hoped to remain unseen by the police. But Johnny knew, and had discovered evidence of Karl’s illegal activities. Winston had a feeling, the city that never slept would soon reveal its hidden truths.

He sighed, dipping under the awning and pushing open the heavy door. The dusky light spilling over worn floorboards greeted him, along with the riotous cacophony of live music. Winston moved on. " I heard from Letti, she’d invited you for a song recording at her isolated mountain cabin, which you're staying at for the duration of the recording."

Eddie nodded. “Yes, it was a wonderful opportunity. Her mountain cabin is beautifully isolated, which makes it an inspiring place especially when you're used to the solitude of camping.”

"I heard you're someone who enjoys a robust collection of wildlife taxidermy," Winston shifted the topic.

Eddie’s face lit up, “Yes, I’ve got a whole room full of specimens at my place, even from endangered species. Interesting how life becomes art with death.”

The interview was interrupted by a growing chorus of fans demanding another performance. Eddie nodded to Winston, picked up his machete, and slipped away. The very same machete he used during his camping trips for safety, now became a prop in his spectacle. He showed the audience his machete tricks, with cheers accompanying each swift, practiced movement.

Winston withdrew from the place, drowned out by the cheering crowd. He left for the isolation of the night, knowing that his work here wasn't nearly done.

Winston pondered over the details of the case. The victim, Letti, had shared with friends about finding documents that implicated her godmother, Delilah, in illicit activities. She had even voiced her intent to go public, starting with confronting Delilah directly. Witnesses reported the last time anyone saw her, it was when Letti walked right into Delilah's cabin with an unflinching resolve. That forced his hand, leading him straight to Delilah's secluded dwelling.

Perched in a rural area with few other houses for company, the cabin was nestled within a copse of trees. As he approached, he saw Delilah outside. Delilah, who was the sole occupant of the cabin known to neighbours, was regularly seen practising with a machete for security purposes. True to the reports, there she was, swinging the machete with a practiced flair, the sun igniting its path before it landed in the trunk of a tree, vibrating under the force of her strike. Even a novice could tell she was someone who knew her way around a blade.

Having verified her identity, Winston started his interrogation casually, focusing on her peculiar hobby. The queries were about her familiarity with the machete and how she had become so skilled. Delilah responded, her accent echoing with local tones, "I've been using a machete since I was a teenager." She continued, reliving her past, "Father taught me. I've won a few of the local competitions, too. Helps living alone out here, one needs to keep sharp."

Winston noted down her history with the weapon and the regular practise for security. He then moved on to discuss Letti. "Did Letti come here often?" he asked.

She confirmed, "Letti did come often, yes. The last time she came was yesterday." Her face revealed a shift in emotion, recognising the motive behind Winston's questioning. Being keen, he paid heed but continued to be nonchalant.

He then prodded about her lifestyle. "You live all alone out here?"

With a nod, Delilah confirmed the solitary lifestyle as she retrieved her machete from the tree. Winston, in the following silence, surveyed the lush woodland around the cabin — offering privacy and seclusion. They marked a stark dichotomy between peace and potential criminal activity within an authoritarian mind like him.

Trying to read any hint of reaction, he brought up Letti's concern. "Your goddaughter," Winston started, "She was worried about you. She found some documents and directly confronted you about some suspicious activities. She even threatened to make it public."

Delilah went rigid, her gaze darting toward the cabin. Her cabin – Letti's statements to her friends made it clear. Winston caught the twitch in her eyes but decided not to press further. The information gleaned from Delilah filled in gaps of Letti's allegations, driving him closer to the incident's truth on the fateful night. When Wilhelmina is mysteriously slain by a crossbow in her own kitchen, Detective Winston steps in to question the two primary suspects, Isabelle and Nicole, in this chilling murder mystery.

Detective Winston's smoke-filled office was filled with tangible tension as he poured over the curious case of Wilhelmina. The facts at hand seemed to spin an intricate web, but the threads only made sense one at a time. 

Nicole, art collector by profession, was ostensibly the last one to see Wilhelmina. They had been scheduled for a meeting at Nicole's house where Nicole had stayed in all day, in the very kitchen where Wilhelmina had been murdered. Winston studied the eerie photographs of the scene, the brightly lit kitchen contrasted with the grim presence of a crossbow.

Shaking his head to focus, Winston remembered his visit to Nicole's home. Her exclusive medieval-themed art pieces took his breath away, as did her pride. "My treasures," she beamed, pointing grandly to a display case which held a pristine medieval crossbow.

A memory tugged at his mind, it wasn't just the crossbow she was proud of. He recalled a discussion with a bartender, the mention of Nicole's frequent appearances at medieval art auctions. What's more, Nicole had been known to read books on crossbows, and there were even whispers among her acquaintances of her crossbow-shooting practices.

And then there were the rumors, dark whispers that followed Nicole like a specter. It seemed that almost everyone Nicole had been friendly with had died under mysterious circumstances, the very circumstances that were all too familiar to Winston as he studied the police records. 

Too many puzzle pieces, yet somehow connected. Even the seemingly mundane receipt Winston held in his hand felt like a silent hint. Nicole had gone grocery shopping recently and had the forethought to buy the deceased's favorite snacks, her groceries for the day when she'd stayed home, and which now lay untouched on the granite counter.

Winston felt the connection, not clear, yet humming under the surface. What were all these interesting coincidences? Was it pure chance that Nicole collected pieces of art connected to people who lay dead? Or that Wilhelmina, a renowned collector of medieval artifacts including crossbows, was found by a crossbow in her friend's kitchen, a friend who had somehow acquired an authentic crossbow as part of her art collection and stayed home all day?

He picked up the phone, ordered more coffee, and resumed his investigations. An intricate puzzle indeed.

Winston frowned at the laptop screen in front of him, then squinted. A plethora of eBooks on archery and yoga were being sent to Isabelle's inbox, indicating Isabelle received her reading materials digitally. A picture of the cheery-looking Isabelle, beaming next to a massive crossbow, was plastered all over her heavily used social media accounts. The caption boasted of her skills, "So proud to be part of the city archery club." He navigated to a different tab, confirming her membership of an online archery club that used crossbows.

As he studied her profile, he noted some details in her bio that surprised him slightly. Next to the information that she was a yoga instructor, it read, "Travel junkie! Always out exploring after each teaching contract!" She had also listed her LinkedIn, which Winston opened. He grimaced as he skimmed over her numerous long-term contracts in various cities, and her preferred methods of payment were invariably digital.

Determined to get a clearer picture of Isabelle, he called her up.

“Isabelle, this is Detective Winston. I’d like to ask you a few questions about the death of Wilhelmina. I’d like to meet in person,” he said.

“I’d prefer if we chat online, Detective. I’m more comfortable that way,” she replied, again indicating her strong preference for online communication.

Hours later, on a video call, Isabelle appeared composed but slightly guarded. 

"Routine is central to my yoga classes, Detective," Isabelle said, and she further explained that her yoga schedule ran like clockwork. The sessions followed a rigid timeslot and it just so happened that the fateful class in Wilhelmina's kitchen took place right around the time of the murder.

"Wilhelmina was a regular attendee in my classes, and she even offered her kitchen for one of our sessions. She thought the atmosphere would be more inviting," Isabelle shared. She paused, seemingly unsure if she should continue. After a beat, she added, "She was a sweet lady. It's sad to think she was murdered right there..."

Her voice trailed off, and she looked the detective square in the face, "I was there, in the kitchen when it happened, but I... I didn’t do anything wrong."

"On the contrary, I just finished up a teaching contract in this city and I look forward to exploring this place more, Detective," she concluded, a half-smile playing on her lips.

After the call ended, Winston sat back in his chair, taking in the conversation. As he switched back to her social media profile, the pictures of her beaming next to her crossbow kept coming back.

A notification chimed, alerting him to a new email from the forensics lab. The report stated that a crossbow could be the murder weapon.

"Interesting," Winston muttered to himself, eyes flicking back to the beaming image of Isabelle and her crossbow on the screen.

The tough soldier, habituated to the brutality of the fight club, would invariably return home every Wednesday morning nursing fresh battle sores.

Alice was a puzzle piece in a complex jigsaw puzzle. An aunt, a loyal fitness center member, a fighter, and undoubtedly an experienced shotgun user due to her military background. Her every Tuesday night fights stood out starkly against her normal routine. She was a conundrum tightly bound by her routine, fitness center membership, military background, and her recent shotgun purchase.
